title: Handlebar Phone Dock
tagline: Turn an old phone into a permanent motorcycle navigation screen.
summary: A slim sealed phone case that slides onto a handlebar dock, locks with a key and charges through spring contacts. No cable to plug in. It fits any motorcycle with a round handlebar (22.2, 25.4 or 28.6 mm) and any phone: set your measurements and export your own parts.
status: a dimensioned concept model, version 0.5. It has not yet been tested on the road, for water, heat or vibration. Check the fit on your own bike and phone before relying on it, and use a safety tether at first.

videos.title: How the locks work: store cam lock, printed push-key lock, dial combination lock

see_sub: The video is rendered straight from the CAD: assembly, docking, the contacts, the wiring, the key lock and the over-heat cut-off.

gallery.caption: The stack: clamps, one-piece dock base, case
The dock base takes the case outline, so from the side case and base read as one slab; the lock sits flush in the side wall
From behind: the lock pod is hidden behind the case's top corner
The dock base: rails, pin pocket, snap arms, clamp slots and the lock pod
Modular option: clamps, base plate on grommets, dock, case (smart base possible later)
Optional printed lock: a chunky 6 x 10 mm push-in key, the shuttle, 4 wafers and their springs
Printed lock cut through a wafer: the key sets its height, and its tab must line up with the groove in the cartridge
One dock, either lock: the store lock in its cartridge, which slides up into the lock bay; the cover holds it in
The printed lock's cartridge fits the same bay
Demo: a mechanical dial lock, numbered 0-9, with a 4-6 digit code. Dial it to unlock; press the button to lock (that also clears the code)
The dial lock's cartridge: a notched wheel per digit, the fence and latch, the spring button with its ramp, the lifter

case_shell.name: Case shell
case_shell.what: Front of the slim case: the window lip, side walls and plug bay

case_back.name: Case back
case_back.what: Back cover: O-ring tongue, cable channel, thermostat pocket

window_template.name: Window template
window_template.what: Guide for cutting the 2 mm polycarbonate window

shoe.name: Shoe
shoe.what: Plate on the case's back: dovetail rails, contact nose, lock strike

dock_base.name: Dock base
dock_base.what: The dock and base plate in one part, shaped to the case outline with side walls: rail channels, pogo-pin pocket, dock-board pocket, printed snap, clamp slots, lock pod (hidden behind the case). Clamp spacing 132–154 mm
dock_base.material: ASA or PETG, on the lock pod's bottom face with supports under the floor

iso_pad.name: Rubber pad
iso_pad.what: Sits between each clamp pad and the dock base; cut from 2 mm neoprene using it as a template, or print it

receiver.name: Dock (modular option)
receiver.what: Modular option (mount = "modular"): the dock on its own, on 4 grommets on the base plate. Use with the modular shoe and back cover
receiver.material: ASA or PETG, printed back face down

base_plate.name: Base plate (modular option)
base_plate.what: Modular option: joins the clamps to the dock through rubber grommets; a smart base can replace it later. Clamp spacing 110–154 mm
base_plate.material: ASA or PETG (or cut from base_plate.dxf)

shoe_modular.name: Shoe (modular option)
shoe_modular.what: The shoe for the modular dock: its strike block is 7 mm higher, to match that dock's lock pod

case_back_modular.name: Case back (modular option)
case_back_modular.what: Back cover for the modular dock: the strike screw inserts are 7 mm higher

strike_keeper_modular.name: Steel keeper (modular option)
strike_keeper_modular.what: Optional steel strike for the modular shoe (steel_keeper = true)

clamp_body.name: Clamp body
clamp_body.material: PETG, ASA or PA12, 100 % infill round the ring

clamp_cap.name: Clamp cap
clamp_cap.material: PETG, ASA or PA12, 100 % infill round the ring

bar_shim.name: Bar shim
bar_shim.what: Adapts the clamps to a smaller bar (or use strips of old inner tube)

pad_spacer.name: Pad spacer
pad_spacer.what: Raises the mount if the instrument cluster needs room

lock_yoke.name: Lock yoke
lock_yoke.what: Carries the steel bolt; driven by the lock's cam

lock_cartridge.name: Lock cartridge
lock_cartridge.what: Holds the 16 mm store lock: slides up into the dock's lock bay, its face plate flush in the side wall. The lock's nut clamps its face plate
lock_cartridge.material: ASA or PETG, 100 % infill, standing on its bottom

lock_cover.name: Lock cover
lock_cover.what: Closes the lock pod and holds the cartridge in (screwed into it), with drain slots. The same for both locks

crank_template.name: Crank template
crank_template.what: Drilling guide for the crank-pin hole in the lock's cam

strike_keeper.name: Steel keeper
strike_keeper.what: Optional steel strike; cut it from strike_keeper_2d.dxf (set steel_keeper = true)

plock_cartridge.name: Printed lock: cartridge
plock_cartridge.what: Use it instead of lock_cartridge if you print the lock: the key slot, the shuttle's channel and the wafer groove. It fits the standard dock
plock_cartridge.material: ASA or PETG, 100 % infill, standing on its bottom

plock_shuttle.name: Printed lock: shuttle
plock_shuttle.what: Slides 7 mm when the key is pushed; carries the 4 wafers and the track that lowers the bolt
plock_shuttle.material: PETG or ASA, 100 % infill, standing on its bottom

plock_lifter.name: Printed lock: lifter
plock_lifter.what: Carries the steel bolt (replaces lock_yoke); its pin runs in the shuttle's track
plock_lifter.material: PA12 or PETG, 100 % infill, standing on its bottom

plock_wafer_1.name: Printed lock: wafer 1
plock_wafer_1.what: Front wafer. The 4 wafers differ (their windows set the key code): print your own from lock_code

plock_wafers.name: Printed lock: all 4 wafers
plock_wafers.what: The 4 wafers on one plate, in order

dl_cartridge.name: Dial lock (demo): cartridge
dl_cartridge.what: Holds the wheels on its fixed tube, the fence, button and lifter; use it instead of lock_cartridge
dl_cartridge.material: PETG or ASA, standing on its bottom

dl_wheel_1.name: Dial lock (demo): wheel 1
dl_wheel_1.what: One wheel per digit; its notch sets the digit (example code here, print your own). Wheel 1 is next to the dial

dl_spindle.name: Dial lock (demo): spindle
dl_spindle.what: Turns with the dial; its drive cam picks up the wheels
dl_spindle.material: PETG or PA12, 100 % infill, on its side

dl_dial.name: Dial lock (demo): dial
dl_dial.material: PETG or ASA, face down, fine layers

dl_fence.name: Dial lock (demo): fence
dl_fence.what: Rises into the wheels' notches at the right code; its printed springy latch arm holds the button in

dl_hammer.name: Dial lock (demo): reset hammer
dl_hammer.what: Lifted by a hump in the button's groove; presses the front wheel's heart cam to clear the code

dl_plunger.name: Dial lock (demo): button
dl_plunger.what: Push button: its ramp lifts the bolt, its notch takes the latch

dl_lifter.name: Dial lock (demo): lifter
dl_lifter.what: Carries the steel bolt (replaces lock_yoke); its pin rides on the button's ramp

plock_key.name: Printed lock: key
plock_key.what: Chunky 6 x 10 mm key with rounded fillets at the bow, pushed straight in (cut to lock_code: the example code here, make your own)

dxf.base_plate: Modular option: the base plate as a flat outline, for cutting from sheet instead of printing
dxf.strike_keeper_2d_modular: Optional 6 mm steel strike for the modular shoe, for laser cutting
dxf.strike_keeper_2d: Optional 6 mm steel strike, for laser cutting (set steel_keeper = true)

download_note: The STLs are made for the default (placeholder) phone, 75 × 160 × 9 mm, and a 22.2 mm handlebar. For your own phone and bike, change the measurements in the source and export your own parts: see Adjust it to your hardware. The parts that depend on the phone are case_shell, case_back and window_template; the clamps and shims depend on the bar.
